On this page

**Koodisi AI** is an AI-powered assistant embedded directly into the Koodisi workspace. You can ask it questions, have it build workflows and mappings, generate documentation, and investigate what went wrong — without leaving the canvas.

You remain responsible for reviewing generated content, testing changes, and deciding what enters an application.

## Where to start [​](https://docs.koodisi.com/nxagent-user-guide/\#where-to-start "Direct link to Where to start")

[**Use Koodisi AI chat** \\
Open the panel, choose a mode, attach context, and review what it proposes.\\
Start here→](https://docs.koodisi.com/nxagent-user-guide/using-nxagent-chat/) [**Build workflows and mappings** \\
Generate a workflow or a data mapping from a plain-language description.\\
Build something→](https://docs.koodisi.com/nxagent-user-guide/building-workflows-and-mappings/) [**Investigate health** \\
Ask why something is failing and get real figures from live data.\\
Investigate→](https://docs.koodisi.com/nxagent-user-guide/investigating-integration-health/)

## Two kinds of AI feature [​](https://docs.koodisi.com/nxagent-user-guide/\#two-kinds-of-ai-feature "Direct link to Two kinds of AI feature")

Koodisi AI's features reach you in two different ways, and knowing which is which saves you looking in the wrong place.

| Kind | How you use it |
| --- | --- |
| Chat features | You ask for them in the Koodisi AI panel |
| In-place features | They live on their own control in the screen where they apply |

## Keep people in control [​](https://docs.koodisi.com/nxagent-user-guide/\#keep-people-in-control "Direct link to Keep people in control")

- Review **Preview** and **Diff** before accepting a generated change.
- Test generated workflows and schemas with representative, non-sensitive data.
- Keep **Auto-accept changes** off for shared applications, unfamiliar tasks, and release-critical work.
- Treat generated explanations as guidance. Verify operational and security decisions against the application and your organization's policies.
- Use the smallest useful context. Remove unrelated workflows and schemas before sending a request.

warning

Do not include passwords, tokens, keys, or customer data in a prompt. Store sensitive values as `secret` variables instead.
